inputs.original_text: Bloomberg’s own framing gives the game away: as energy prices rise, flights are canceled, and death and destruction dominate the screens, people worldwide are asking when the Iran war will stop. Yet Israel is presented as the exception, with strong public backing to see it through. That contrast is doing useful work: it makes an ongoing war sound like public resolve rather than a choice being sustained by powerful interests. The account doesn’t even finish the thought after “until,” but the omission only sharpens the question of who benefits from keeping this going.
inputs.modified_text: Bloomberg’s framing is the tell: while rising energy prices, canceled flights, and death and destruction make people worldwide ask when the Iran war will stop, Israel is cast as uniquely willing to keep going. That contrast turns continuation into “public resolve” and hides the interests that may be sustaining it. And the account cuts off after “until”—an omission that leaves the real question hanging: who benefits from keeping this war going?
